newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala regrets CIA documents withholds names.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala regrets CIA documents withholds names.

text.p: Guatemala said on Sunday it regretted that the names of those involved with CIA plots to destabilise the Guatemalean government in the 1950s were blacked out in previously secret CIA documents released late last week.

"Last Friday we received a copy of the documents that were made public in Washington concerning the views of the CIA..., at the time that President Jaco Arbenz Guzman was overthrown," said Foreign Affairs Minister Eduardo Stein.
"Unfortunately they have kept secret the names of the North American agents and the Guatemalan politicians that were involved. All the documents block out this data," he said.

The U.S. spy agency said last Friday that senior Central Intelligence Agency officials mulled plots to assassinate scores of Guatemalan leaders as part of a 1954 coup against the elected government. No killings were ever approved or carried out.
The CIA acknowledged that "some actual preparations were made," including the training of some exiled Guatemalan hit-men.

One newly declassified document mentioned 58 Guatemalans as possible assassination targets because of their association with President Jacobo Arbenz Guzman, a social reformer ousted in the putsch carried out under President Dwight Eisenhower.

The CIA, fighting to check expansion of Communism, moved against Arbenz after he legalised the Communist Party, invited it to join his government and expropriated nearly 400,000 acres of banana plantations owned by the United Fruit Company of the United States.
In late June 1954, under the pressure of a CIA-backed paramilitary action, the Arbenz government collapsed.
Names of those mentioned as possible assassination targets were blacked out in the declassified files of CIA operations codenamed Fortune, Success and History.
Also blacked out were the names of CIA officers and others involved.
